title: This Eagles offensive lineman admits he was ‘a complete liability’ and needed to be shut down
content:
The Philadelphia Eagles are placing left guard Landon Dickerson on injured reserve.

Dickerson confirmed while speaking on his Monday night radio show on 94.1 WIP that the Eagles informed him of their plan to place him on injured reserve. Dickerson said he has bone bruising in his right knee. He said he was told it would not heal if he kept “banging it up,” and that he needed to shut it down and let it heal.

Dickerson, who must miss at least four games, said the Eagles want to allow time for his knee to recover so he can return later this season.

The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane first reported that Dickerson was heading to injured reserve.

Dickerson, 27, said the bone bruising is a new injury. He said he was not in the locker room for postgame interviews after Sunday’s 24-22 win over the Washington Commanders because he was checking in with team doctors. Dickerson stressed the importance of getting healthy and took responsibility for having played “like s—.” His mobility was limited against Washington, particularly in pass protection.

Dickerson, who has undergone nearly a dozen surgeries in his career for various injuries, emphasized that he intends to continue playing upon his return. He traveled to Colombia in the offseason to undergo stem cell therapy. If he had been considering retirement, “I wouldn’t have spent seven figures in the offseason,” he said.

Dickerson said in August that he will not try to play through injuries as he did in previous seasons.

“I don’t think there’s any reason to be tough and play through it if it’s just going to wear you down,” Dickerson said. “They don’t pay me to be hurt.”

Drew Kendall and Willie Lampkin are next in line to start in Dickerson’s absence. Both had promising training camps.
